abstract: Site-specific recombinases, such as Cre recombinase (Cre) and FLP recombinase (FLPase), are popular tools that enable precise spatiotemporal control over fluorescent reporter genes. However, studies show that increased Cre expression can lead to cytotoxic phenotypes including DNA damage, cell cycle arrest, cell death, and aneuploidy. In contrast, there is little-to-no known cytotoxicity associated with FLPase. FLPase is considered to be the safer, if less efficient, recombinase. To compensate for decreased efficiency, researchers will often increase expression of the FLPase to ensure a complete gene edit. Despite previous evidence that FLPase is nontoxic at high doses, we report that high expression of FLPase from multi-copy extrachromosomal arrays can disrupt synaptic protein trafficking in C. elegans. We discovered several off-target effects of high FLPase expression including mislocalization of the pre-synaptic marker FLPon::mScarlet::SYD-2 and decreased synaptic abundance, transport, and expression of the ionotropic glutamate receptor subunit GLR-1 in AVA command interneurons. Neither overexpression of an inactive FLPase, low activity FLPase, nor mCherry under the same promoter elicits these effects. Further, single-copy expression of the FLPase construct reliably tags FLPon::mScarlet::SYD-2 and does not lead to these off-target effects. This work supports growing awareness that tyrosine recombinases can become cytotoxic at high doses.
